title: A Thousand Mountains | Suspended, Drowning
subtitle: I am beginning to love the feeling of drowning: suspended, drifting, seeking no final home.
body:
It is not that you do not understand when I say I love you How can one breathe underwater? Only when I sink to the seabed do I become clearheaded Love is not a competitive game I think I love you They are not merely words The pressure in my lungs Turns to bubbles in the next second and disappears Breathing underwater In time with synchronized heartbeats Perhaps I am not clever enough To understand when you say love needs no proof
My heart is a bird of the wilderness Yet in your eyes there is a sky Your breath is the wind among the mountains I soar and fall, utterly free No trace can be seen But I have flown
I pretend to leave Waving my sleeve, taking not a single cloud away[1] Yet I fall again Willingly silent on the seabed Seeking no final home I think I am beginning to like floating
The stillness of the seabed Cannot soothe my heart’s trembling I give up words And give up proving that I love you Only enjoying suspension and immersion --- [1] An allusion to the closing lines of Xu Zhimo’s [*Saying Goodbye to Cambridge Again*](https://zh.wikisource.org/zh-hans/再别康桥).
